title: Flat finite-presentation morphisms preserve a dense-open relative dimension bound
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] whose underlying subset is dense, meaning that every nonempty open subset of $S$ meets $U$. Fix an integer $e\geq0$. Let $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projection $f_U:X_U\to U$, and for a morphism $g:Y\to T$ and $t\in T$ write $Y_t$ for the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $\dim_y(Y_{g(y)})$ for the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] of $Y_{g(y)}$ at the point lying over $y\in Y$. If $\dim_x((X_U)_{f_U(x)})\leq e$ for every $x\in X_U$, then $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})\leq e$ for every $x\in X$.

proof.text: First translate the hypothesis over $U$ into a statement about the original fibres: if $s\in U$, then $(X_U)_s\cong X_s$, preserving the point over each $x\in X$ with $f(x)=s$. Indeed the open-subscheme stalk at $s$ is the same stalk as in $S$ (intersections with $U$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods), so its residue field is $\kappa(s)$. Both schemes then represent pairs consisting of a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ agreeing in $S$; the intermediate map to $U$ is forced. The fibre-product universal property gives inverse isomorphisms. Their underlying homeomorphisms identify open neighbourhoods and chains of irreducible closed subsets, hence the defining local dimensions. Consequently $\dim_xX_{f(x)}\leq e$ whenever $f(x)\in U$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-dimension-strata-core] to $f$ and the whole open $S\subseteq S$. Its restriction hypotheses are precisely the given flatness and local finite presentation. Obtain opens $V_n\subseteq X$, $n\in\mathbb N$, such that $W=\bigcup_nV_n$ has dense inverse image in every fibre and $\dim_yX_{f(y)}=n$ at every $y\in V_n$. Put $W_s=(X_s\to X)^{-1}(W)$; this is a dense open subset of $X_s$.

source.place: Tag 054T, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-pieces, and Tag 045U, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-CM-open; the dimension-piece construction invoked in Tag 081L

proof.text: For $n>e$, suppose $V_n$ is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $f(V_n)$ is open in $S$, and it is nonempty because $V_n$ contains a point. Density of $U$ gives an $s\in f(V_n)\cap U$ and then a $y\in V_n$ with $f(y)=s$. Step 2 gives $\dim_yX_s=n$, whereas step 1 gives $\dim_yX_s\leq e$, a contradiction. Thus $V_n=\varnothing$ for $n>e$. Every point of $W_s$ therefore has local dimension in $X_s$ at most $e$, for every $s\in S$.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $x\in X$ and put $s=f(x)$ and $Y=X_s$. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], choose affine opens $x\in V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ and $s\in T=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, with $f(V)\subseteq T$ and $B\cong R[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso] to $z=f$, $t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$, these opens $T,V$, and the rings $R,B,\kappa(s)$. Here $t^{-1}(T)$ is the whole residue-field spectrum since $s\in T$. The lemma identifies the open $A=(Y\to X)^{-1}(V)$, containing the point over $x$, with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\otimes_R B)$. The tensor algebra is generated over $\kappa(s)$ by the $1\otimes t_i$: expand a simple tensor using the polynomial presentation of its second factor, and move coefficients from $R$ into $\kappa(s)$ by the balancing relation. Thus $A$ is an affine scheme of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: Set $H=A\cap W_s$, an open subscheme of $Y$ and of $A$. It is dense in $A$: any nonempty open of $A$ is open in $Y$ because $A$ is open, so it meets the dense subset $W_s$ and the intersection lies in $H$. For $h\in H$, step 3 gives $\dim_hY\leq e$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] to the open inclusion $H\subseteq Y$ to obtain $\dim_hH=\dim_hY\leq e$.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull), item (4) and following neighbourhood discussion; dense open restriction in the fibre

proof.text: For each $h\in H$, the minimum in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is attained, so choose an open neighbourhood $N_h\subseteq H$ with $\dim N_h=\dim_hH\leq e$. These opens cover $H$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $H$ has unique generic points for irreducible closed subsets; this makes it quasi-sober and $T_0$ (points with equal singleton closures must be the same generic point). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] to conclude $\dim H\leq e$. If $H$ is empty, the same lemma applies to the empty cover and gives the same bound. This passage uses only the dimension definition and the cited open-cover theorem, not a bound on the dimensions of local rings.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull), item (4); Tag 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions), open-cover consequence; Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text: The scheme $A$ is of finite type over the field $\kappa(s)$ by step 4, and $H\hookrightarrow A$ is open dense by step 5. The dense-open clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim A=\dim H\leq e$; the symbol $\kundim$ in that node is the same topological Krull dimension by [def-kun-dimension]. At the point $\widetilde x\in A$ over $x$, the whole open $A$ is one of its own neighbourhoods, so [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim_{\widetilde x}A\leq\dim A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] to $A\subseteq Y$ to conclude $\dim_xX_s=\dim_{\widetilde x}Y=\dim_{\widetilde x}A\leq e$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, this is the assertion. Empty $X$ has no such $x$ and is covered vacuously.
